Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada told reporters last week that her husband, who is Black, had been repeatedly stopped by police while driving.

So when the email titled “June Holiday” arrived in thousands of inboxes, they felt a moment of overdue joy.

Police in Vietnam have rescued more than 400 cats in a bust of a cat meat crime ring in Ho Chi Minh City, according to animal welfare groups and local media reports.

More than 40 cats were reunited with their owners after the multiday operation last week, but several dozen of those rescued have died due to the harsh conditions in which they were found, the groups said.

rfi.title: France scrambles to respond, as June heatwave grips Europe
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to hold a crisis meeting on Tuesday, after Météo France reported that the country's average temperature had broken a June record. Elsewhere in Europe, several countries are also struggling with the heatwave, which has led to a number of deaths and disruption to public services.

rfi.title: EU gambles on Taliban talks to fast-track Afghan deportations
rfi.description: A Taliban delegation is due to fly into Brussels on Tuesday, having been granted a one-day visa to hold talks with the EU on returning failed asylum seekers to Afghanistan. However, human rights groups have warned that the scheme runs counter to the bloc's values.

rfi.title: Blood minerals and memory: the Great Lakes in focus
rfi.description: This week, Spotlight on Africa turns to the Great Lakes region. First, a new Global Witness report reveals how coltan is being smuggled out of the Democratic Republic of Congo, amid the ongoing conflict in the east, through Rwanda and on to companies worldwide. Then, artist Grada Kilomba discusses her journey to create a unique monument for Paris commemorating the 1994 Rwandan genocide.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: 'Export trade has increased since exiting the EU, it's been a win'
rfi.description: Ten years after the United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union, Brexit remains one of the most contested political decisions in recent British history. Its legacy is increasingly shaped by diverging interpretations of sovereignty and the UK's place in the world. RFI spoke to Brexit supporter Robert Oulds, director of British think tank the Bruges Group, about what has changed.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: the promises, the costs and the search for accountability
rfi.description: Ten years on, the UK's decision to leave the European Union is increasingly seen as more than a single referendum result. Critics argue it reflected a wider crisis of political imagination, with Brexit supporters misreading both Britain and the world, while the promised future never arrived.

rfi.title: Resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch enters Paris's Pantheon
rfi.description: French resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch will be inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on Tuesday, giving President Emmanuel Macron another chance to shape France’s national memory through one of the Republic’s most symbolic ceremonies.

rfi.title: Mbappé's double on 100th appearance fires France into World Cup knockout stages
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé marked his 100th cap for France on Monday night with two goals in their 3-0 win over Iraq in a game that took more than four hours to complete due to thunder storms over Philadelphia.

rfi.title: Messi notches up World Cup goals record to take Argentina into knockout stages
rfi.description: Argentina skipper Lionel Messi added another accolade to his otherworldly list of achievements on Monday when he became the record goalscorer at World Cups since the inception of the tournament in 1930

rfi.title: Haaland scores twice as Norway outwit Senegal to reach last 32 at World Cup
rfi.description: Erling Haaland scored twice on Monday night as Norway advanced to the knockout stages at the World Cup following a pulsating 3-2 victory over Senegal in New Jersey.

rfi.title: Repeated errors in handling of rape case linked to French girl's death: report
rfi.description: An administrative investigation ordered after the death of 11 year-old Lyhanna in southern France has revealed serious failings in how a previous rape complaint against the main suspect was handled. The case has brought the French judicial and police system under stark scrutiny, especially regarding cases of child abuse.

rfi.title: 'Poison in your coffee' report sounds alarm over widespread pesticide use
rfi.description: Coffee production around the world depends heavily on pesticides, leaving millions of farm workers exposed to harmful chemicals while pesticide residues are also found in exported coffee beans, a report published on Monday warned.

rfi.title: Paris court rejects bid to reopen probe into Caribbean chlordecone contamination
rfi.description: The Paris appeals court has upheld a decision not to reopen a criminal investigation into the use of chlordecone, a toxic pesticide that has been linked to cancer and other health problems in around 90 percent of the adult population in Guadeloupe and Martinique.

rfi.title: UN warns of an 'imminent risk of mass atrocities' in Sudan's Kordofan
rfi.description: In Sudan, NGOs and the UN have warned of an "imminent risk of mass atrocities" in El-Obeid, a major city in North Kordofan. This comes as the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) step up their campaign against the regular army in the region.

rfi.title: France, Germany reach deal on arms maker KNDS, opening door to stock market
rfi.description: France and Germany announced Monday a deal for the joint governance of Amsterdam-headquartered arms maker KNDS, paving the way for a blockbuster share offering as they seek to boost faltering European defence cooperation.

rfi.title: France's scorching weekend heat leads to elderly deaths and spate of drownings
rfi.description: The deaths of three elderly people in southwestern France have been linked to the heatwave hitting the country, while authorities have reported an increase in drownings, as people seek relief from the heat in rivers and lakes.

rfi.title: UK's Starmer resigns as prime minister
rfi.description: UK leader Keir Starmer announced his resignation on Monday following months of pressure, kickstarting a process that will see Britain get its seventh prime minister in a decade.

rfi.title: DRC announces free healthcare for all illnesses in Ituri as Ebola gains ground
rfi.description: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has announced the introduction of free healthcare for all diseases in Ituri – a pilot project that authorities hope to extend nationwide. This comes as the country struggles to contain an Ebola outbreak, with confirmed cases now at over 1,000.

rfi.title: Ethiopia’s ruling party wins another large majority in parliament
rfi.description: Ethiopia's ruling party has won over 90 percent of seats in parliament, according to official results announced three weeks after the election.

euronews.title: UNAIDS warns Trump's HIV funding cuts to South Africa could cost lives
euronews.description: The Trump administration says the phased withdrawal is linked to policy disputes with Pretoria, which rejects the allegations and says it is pursuing greater self-reliance.

euronews.title: Nicotine pouch sales surge among young people, watchdog warns
euronews.description: Flavoured, promoted on social media, discreet and unregulated: sales of addictive nicotine pouches are booming among youth. A global tobacco industry watchdog, STOP, warns that this could lead to a new wave of nicotine addiction.

euronews.title: Iceland kills first whales since 2023, resuming whaling
euronews.description: Iceland's Marine and Freshwater Research Institute has recommended that no more than 150 fin whales are caught in the 2026 season.

euronews.title: Japan's emperor and empress arrive in Belgium for state visit
euronews.description: The arrival of Japan's emperor and empress in Belgium marks a symbolic moment for two countries whose partnership stretches back more than a century and a half.

euronews.title: Von der Leyen to visit Pashinyan in Yerevan to build on Armenia’s pro-EU vote
euronews.description: As the EU rolls out a support package for Armenia, European Commission President von der Leyen is set to meet re-elected Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan in Yerevan after he secured a decisive pro-West mandate from the Armenian people, sources confirmed to Euronews.

euronews.title: UN launches Hormuz evacuation for 11,000 stranded seafarers
euronews.description: The operation follows a peace agreement between the United States and Iran that ended months of conflict and allowed commercial shipping to resume through one of the world's most important maritime routes.

euronews.description: EU officials and Taliban representatives held a technical meeting in Brussels to discuss the return of Afghan nationals in a fresh attempt to ramp up repatriations of migrants without the right to stay in Europe.

euronews.title: From Bolsonaro and Bukele to Fujimori and De la Espriella: Trump and Latin America's rightward turn
euronews.description: Soon after the US president first moved into the White House, his policies and outspoken backing for certain candidates inspired a new wave of Latin American leaders now shaping the continent’s future.

euronews.title: LEGO's Julia Goldin named first-ever European CMO of the Year at Cannes Lions
euronews.description: Chosen by more than 800 marketing leaders from across Europe, Julia Goldin was recognised for helping transform LEGO into a global cultural brand through partnerships spanning entertainment, gaming and sport.

euronews.title: Armenia and Azerbaijan agree landmark internet deal as peace process continues
euronews.description: Armenia and Azerbaijan’s leading telecom companies agreed to a joint internet transit project as both countries move forward together after decades of war, boosting regional connectivity.

euronews.title: Versailles unveils gallery for 250th anniversary of US independence
euronews.description: Opening on Saturday 4 July, this gallery brings together paintings, sculptures and portraits from the château’s collections to spotlight the political, diplomatic and military figures of independence.

euronews.title: How Israel became a test case for the EU's institutional battle over foreign policy
euronews.description: Diverging views on the EU's relations with Israel are exposing a growing rivalry between the European Commission and top diplomat Kaja Kallas over who sets the bloc's foreign policy, undermining its overall coherence.

euronews.title: Spain toughens rules for e-scooters: new requirements
euronews.description: The government has approved a reform to the General Traffic Regulations making helmets compulsory for e-scooter users nationwide and setting a minimum age of 15. The measure forms part of a road safety package.

euronews.title: Ukraine says key Crimea rail bridge ‘no longer exists’ after drone strikes
euronews.description: Ukraine said it struck a major blow to Russia’s grip on the occupied Crimean peninsula, announcing the destruction of a key railway bridge over the North Crimean Canal in a series of strikes. The bridge is the “first one” to be eliminated, Kyiv’s troops said.

euronews.title: Kubilius: Europe should prepare for ‘more’ attacks following suspected targeted killing in Poland
euronews.description: The EU’s defence chief has cautioned that Moscow will continue provoking Europe as it falters on the frontlines, particularly after the high-profile death of an exiled Russian citizen critical of Putin living in Poland.

euronews.title: At least 20 drownings reported as 54 French departments remain on red alert
euronews.description: After an exceptionally hot day yesterday, with temperatures above 40°C in some cities, the heatwave continues: 54 départements are on red alert this Tuesday 23 June in France.

euronews.title: Fire at animation studio in India kills at least 15 people
euronews.description: The fire happened in a building housing a student training centre in northern India, raising fresh concerns about fire safety in the country.

lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », le ministre expose les points-clés de son projet de loi destiné à augmenter l’offre d’habitations et présenté, mercredi, en conseil des ministres, et esquisse des pistes pour faire face aux canicules.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Marc Bloch au Panthéon : Emmanuel Macron et de nombreuses personnalités politiques présentes à la cérémonie d’hommage
lemonde.description: Né à Lyon en 1886 dans une famille juive alsacienne, le résistant et auteur de « L’Etrange Défaite » s’est imposé comme l’un des plus grands historiens français du XXᵉ siècle. Il entre au Panthéon mardi.

lemonde.title: Autonomie de la Corse : le principe a été approuvé par l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: C’est Gérald Darmanin, alors ministre de l’intérieur, qui avait été chargé par Emmanuel Macron de mettre sur pied le projet de loi, pour mettre un terme aux violences provoquées par la mort en prison du militant indépendantiste Yvan Colonna.

lemonde.title: Pour la Chine, la guerre au Moyen-Orient n’a pas engendré de grand choc énergétique
lemonde.description: Fortement dépendant des hydrocarbures du Golfe, Pékin est toutefois parvenu à réduire sa consommation d’or noir depuis les tensions autour du détroit d’Ormuz. En compensant avec le charbon et les énergies vertes, mais aussi en raison de la faiblesse conjoncturelle de son économie.

lemonde.title: Au Soudan, la crainte d’un assaut des paramilitaires sur El-Obeid
lemonde.description: Huit mois après la prise sanglante d’El-Fasher, la capitale du Kordofan du Nord pourrait à son tour tomber aux mains des Forces de soutien rapide. Depuis début juin, les paramilitaires mènent une intense campagne de bombardements aériens sur la ville.

lemonde.title: Portugal-Ouzbékistan : Cristiano Ronaldo, auteur d’un doublé, mène la Seleçao à un succès aisé
lemonde.description: A 41 ans, le quintuple Ballon d’or est devenu le premier joueur à marquer lors de six Coupes du monde consécutives, lors du succès portugais face aux Loups blancs (5-0), mardi à Houston.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : des bombardements russes tuent six personnes dans l’oblast de Dnipropetrovsk
lemonde.description: Le bilan humain des frappes russes sur la ville de Kryvy Rih n’a pas évolué depuis le début de l’après-midi. En revanche, le gouverneur de l’oblast de Dnipropetrovsk, dans lequel elle se situe, a fait état de trois autres personnes tuées et de 32 blessées.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : une « loi intégrale » examinée au Parlement en septembre, annonce Sébastien Lecornu
lemonde.description: Le premier ministre a souligné que le sujet nécessiterait « énormément de travail cet été pour arriver à quelque chose qui soit, au fond, à la hauteur », suggérant que le texte devrait donc être modifié.

lemonde.title: Pesticides : condamné à réviser les autorisations de mise sur le marché, l’Etat propose de réévaluer sept produits, soit 0,28 % des tonnages utilisés
lemonde.description: Les associations à l’origine de l’affaire « Justice pour le vivant » vont de nouveau aller devant le tribunal pour dénoncer les « insuffisances » du plan d’action du gouvernement en matière d’évaluation des risques des pesticides, auquel « Le Monde » a eu accès.

lemonde.title: « L’étagère du bas, c’est ma salle de bains » : le 10 mètres carrés parisien de Léa, toute jeune avocate
lemonde.description: « Et toi, t’habites où ? ». En pleine crise du logement, étudiants et jeunes actifs redéfinissent, souvent malgré eux, l’art de trouver un chez-soi. Cette semaine, Léa, 28 ans, originaire de Tours, raconte son attachement à son 10 mètres carrés, sans lequel elle n’aurait pas pu faire ses études de droit à la Sorbonne.

lemonde.title: Les déboires d’Ilia Traber, le mafieux de Saint-Pétersbourg qui doit beaucoup à Vladimir Poutine
lemonde.description: Réputé intouchable grâce à ses liens noués avec le président russe, dès les années 1990, « l’antiquaire », son surnom au sein de la pègre, a été arrêté le 17 juin et inculpé de meurtre organisé. Sa chute met en lumière l’enjeu que constitue, pour l’Etat, le contrôle des ports stratégiques du nord-ouest de la Russie.

lemonde.title: Trésor de la Chouette d’or : un détracteur de la célèbre chasse au trésor devant la justice
lemonde.description: Gérard Simon, président de l’Association des chercheurs de la Chouette d’or, avait remis en cause les solutions au jeu de piste commencé en 1993, allant jusqu’à déposer plainte pour « escroquerie en bande organisée ».

lemonde.title: La mezzo-soprano Coline Dutilleul fait briller les étoiles dans le ciel noir de Schubert
lemonde.description: Avec « In deinen süssen Händen », la chanteuse belge livre un lumineux album où des lieder de Franz Schubert sur le thème de la mort voisinent avec des pièces pour clavier de Jean-Sébastien Bach.

lemonde.title: Sylvie Gir, secrétaire générale des députés de droite et dernière chiraquienne de l’Assemblée, prend sa retraite
lemonde.description: Après quarante ans au Palais-Bourbon, la « SG » du groupe Droite républicaine sera remplacée par un proche de Laurent Wauquiez. Si elle n’était pas élue, elle a œuvré par conviction et fut une cheville ouvrière de la droite parlementaire.

lemonde.title: « Le Brexit a clairement un impact négatif sur l’économie britannique », assure Sarah Hall, de l’université de Cambridge
lemonde.description: Les exportations de biens et les secteurs employant de nombreux Européens ont été les plus durement touchés par la sortie de l’Union européenne, explique la géographe économique, dans un entretien au « Monde ». Le Royaume-Uni a récemment amorcé un rapprochement avec Bruxelles.

lemonde.title: Le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU veut que les auteurs d’attaques meurtrières contre des casques bleus soient mieux poursuivis
lemonde.description: « Les soldats de la paix sont pris pour cible, souvent sans que les responsables aient à rendre des comptes », selon l’ambassadeur pakistanais à l’origine de cette résolution. Ces derniers mois, des casques bleus ont été tués au Liban et au Soudan.

These chemical, physical and electrical messages help determine when cells grow, repair damage, fight infection or quiet down after a threat has passed—and tissue health depends on how well those parts come together.

phys-org.description: In a primary school classroom, a 9-year-old reads aloud to the person next to them. When they stumble over a word, their partner encourages them to try again. Together, they discuss what might happen next. But the child isn't reading to an adult—a teaching assistant or volunteer. Instead, they are reading to a peer in their class. Later, they'll switch jobs and help their partner out as they read.

phys-org.description: Patterns reveal the individual: A novel AI algorithm equips researchers with a powerful new tool to accurately identify individual jaguars, zebras and giraffes in real time based on their unique coat patterns. phys-org.title: Hundreds of schools close as UK braces for record-breaking heat wave

phys-org.title: Ten Australians are taking the government to the UN over fossil fuel exports. What is their case?
phys-org.description: Ten Australians—including a firefighter, First Nations leaders and young people—are bringing their concerns about the nation's coal and gas exports to the United Nations. phys-org.title: Researchers find microplastics in hedgehogs—then trace them back to pet food
phys-org.description: When colleagues and I found microplastics in hedgehog droppings, we wanted to know where they were coming from. One answer was surprisingly close to home: pet food.

phys-org.title: What is driving Europe's heat wave?
phys-org.description: Europe is baking under a scorching heat wave, with health warnings in place across Western and Central Europe as temperatures climb to record-breaking highs.

phys-org.title: Europe: the world's fastest-warming continent
phys-org.description: The latest heat wave sweeping across Europe is a stark reminder that it is the world's fastest-warming continent, stretching into an Arctic that is heating at an even greater pace.

phys-org.title: India monsoon sweeps north but brings less rain than usual
phys-org.description: Long-awaited monsoon rains arrived in India's financial capital, Mumbai, on Tuesday, cooling weeks of blazing heat despite persistent fears of water shortages, with total rainfall so far staying below the long-term average.

phys-org.title: Happy Asteroid Day! Prize-winning plan focuses on space infrastructure
phys-org.description: For decades, astronomers and policymakers have been working on plans to protect our planet from killer asteroids. But now there's a new realm to protect: the thousands of satellites we're putting in orbit.

phys-org.description: Polystyrene—common in packing peanuts and box inserts—is manufactured from fossil fuels. phys-org.title: How a heat dome is formed and why experts blame one for Europe's baking temperatures
phys-org.description: Europe is sizzling under an early heat wave this week, with millions of people experiencing extremely high temperatures, and experts say a phenomenon known as a heat dome is to blame.

phys-org.title: Yellow mealworms mapped anatomically for the first time
phys-org.description: The dried larvae of the yellow mealworm beetle (Tenebrio molitor) are comparable to beef or poultry in nutritional value, but the mealworm has a far smaller ecological footprint. It was recently approved for human consumption by the European Food Safety Authority.

phys-org.title: Pathway to high-fidelity quantum computing identified
phys-org.description: Researchers from the University of Sydney, working with IBM, have identified and quantified important factors limiting the performance of quantum computers and demonstrated ways to overcome their impact.

new-sci.title: SpaceX's secretive plans to deliver cargo to Earth from space
new-sci.description: Not much is known about Starfall, SpaceX's new delivery system, but an assessment published in May revealed its intended purpose

new-sci.title: How some people's brains make an extraordinary recovery from stroke
new-sci.description: Around a third of people are able to almost fully rebuild their brains after a stroke and uncovering why is pointing the way to better treatments for everyone

new-sci.description: A woman with severe Alzheimer's disease who hadn't spoken more than monosyllables in years began initiating conversation after a single dose of psilocybin

new-sci.title: The surprising ways your brain changes from your 20s to your 40s
new-sci.description: When does your brain reach adulthood? We're now understanding the many ways the organ continues to mature decades after society first deems you an adult

new-sci.title: People training new AI models admit they just get chatbots to do it
new-sci.description: The next generation of AI models are meant to be trained by people paid to have conversations with them, but several of these workers have admitted to New Scientist that they simply get chatbots to do it instead. new-sci.title: We've found a mysterious substance on Titan and Pluto
new-sci.description: Something is absorbing light on the surfaces of Pluto and Saturn’s moon Titan, and figuring out what it is could be crucial to understanding Titan’s complex chemistry

new-sci.title: Autism may have two distinct subtypes that vary by brain activity
new-sci.description: Evidence is mounting that there are distinct subtypes of autism, and now, scientists have found that the condition can vary according to the strength of people's brain connections

new-sci.title: A quantum state that lasts forever may finally be within our grasp
new-sci.description: Defying the laws of thermodynamics, experiments are beginning to show that a quantum state that is frozen forever might not be impossible. If we can tame it, it could unlock whole new types of matter

new-sci.title: The one film to watch before seeing Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day
new-sci.description: With Steven Spielberg’s new extraterrestrial film Disclosure Day just out, it’s the ideal time to watch Close Encounters of the Third Kind – perhaps the perfect UFO film, says film columnist Bethan Ackerley

new-sci.title: Faecal transplant makes the brains of old mice act young again
new-sci.description: Older mice that received a faecal microbiome transplant from younger animals went on to have improved brain plasticity, which suggests their brains could overcome a neurological condition that is typically successfully treated only in childhood

new-sci.title: Most portable air conditioners suck – but there's an easy fix
new-sci.description: Efficiency ratings on portable air conditioners don’t give consumers the full picture, and one type of aircon unit is so inefficient that it should be banned, says Michael Le Page

new-sci.title: Has the answer to life's origins been hiding in our cells all along?
new-sci.description: The surprising discovery of mysterious blobs inside our cells is revolutionising our understanding of how life works, and how it got started

new-sci.title: Gas from Uranus reveals it has an icy centre
new-sci.description: Carbon monoxide in Uranus's deep atmosphere indicates that the planet contains more ice than rock, suggesting it formed more like Neptune than we thought

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.
